title: Remote Authentication Dial In User Service (RADIUS)

provenance.original_holder: IETF RADIUS/NASREQ standards process with Livingston/Merit participants

claims_extracted.claim: RADIUS was originally developed by Livingston Enterprises for its PortMaster series of Network Access Servers.
claims_extracted.locator: Acknowledgments, RFC 2058 page 63 / lines 3457-3460 in RFC Editor HTML
claims_extracted.notes: Direct product-to-protocol ancestry statement from the standards document.

claims_extracted.claim: The motivating operational problem is centralized administration, security and service configuration for dispersed serial-line/modem pools serving many users.
A Network Access Server acts as a RADIUS client, passing user information to servers and acting on returned authentication/service configuration.
RADIUS uses extensible variable-length Attribute-Length-Value information and includes framed access, IP, LAT and authentication attributes.
claims_extracted.locator: Section 1 Extensible Protocol and Section 5 Attributes
claims_extracted.notes: The attribute inventory is an archaeological snapshot of a multiprotocol access-server era.

notes: Crucial primary source because it states the protocol's Livingston/PortMaster origin explicitly rather than requiring retrospective inference.
